newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tax break seen for using Western accounting.
newsitem.headline: Russia tax break seen for using Western accounting.

text.p: Russia will introduce tax breaks or other incentives by the end of the year for companies using international accounting methods as part of a new business reform plan, Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Wednesday.

"Companies which follow these (international accounting) standards will have their profit taxes lowered by, say, five percent... or maybe they will recieve other privileges," Yasin told the American Chamber of Commerce.
He predicted the four-year plan under development would be enacted by the administration by the end of the year.
Most Russian companies use domestic accounting practices developed to calculate tax levels. Western accountants say Russian accounting has limited use for business planning and investment.
Yasin said the new plan would motivate businesses to voluntarily change their business practices, though he said the changes were necessary for the health of Russian companies.
"Companies will have to change their management and asset management practices to work more effectively," he added.
